subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram slash sessions still resolve to channel=(unknown), causing elevated allowFrom checks to fail on 2026.3.13

question: Should OpenClaw port the mergeable fork approach for `telegram:slash:<id>` sandbox explain, or require a narrower diagnostic-only fix before changing elevated allowFrom channel resolution?
rationale: The remaining bug sits on elevated authorization diagnostics, and source inspection proves the gap, but the permanent boundary between slash command session keys, target sessions, and runtime authorization needs maintainer/security intent before automation should change it.

options.title: Port a narrow diagnostic fix
options.body: Repair `sandbox explain` for documented Telegram native slash keys while keeping runtime elevated authorization tied to `Provider` and `CommandTargetSessionKey`, with focused tests and Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt the mergeable fork PR
options.body: Review and port `https://github.com/BingqingLyu/openclaw/pull/1143` if maintainers accept wrapping non-agent-scoped colon keys for this diagnostic path.

options.title: Wait for live runtime proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer can prove whether current Telegram elevated runtime still fails beyond the diagnostic path.

recommendation.title: Port a narrow diagnostic fix
recommendation.body: Repair `sandbox explain` for documented Telegram native slash keys while keeping runtime elevated authorization tied to `Provider` and `CommandTargetSessionKey`, with focused tests and Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Bartok9 is the strongest current-code routing candidate because the inspected current files blame to their squashed PR commit.
